channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] France expects EU sanctions within a month over Iran’s refrigeration sabotage as Iran-linked hackers turn to physical attacks
item.description: France’s foreign minister said on 17 November that EU sanctions on the people behind October’s sabotage of supermarket refrigeration controllers could come within a month, freezing their assets and barring travel, a day after EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas confirmed new Iran sanctions are being prepared. Paris blames the IRGC’s Shahid Kaveh unit for the attack on about 700 French sites, which French authorities say caused at least 15 fires, and has sought arrest warrants for three officers; Iran rejects the accusations. Health-ISAC warned on 16 November that settings were also changed at French blood-service sites, putting donor blood and therapies at risk. US and Israeli officials have told the Wall Street Journal that Iran-linked hackers also sabotaged equipment at small Midwest water stations and aboard two tankers. For OT defenders the lesson is plain: any internet-reachable controller is now a proven target. - APA (18 Nov 2026, Barrot on France 5: sanctions within a month); dpa, via Yahoo News (16 Nov 2026, Kallas: EU sanctions in preparation); Asharq Al-Awsat and The New Arab (16 Nov 2026, French sanctions push); Health-ISAC (16 Nov 2026, cold-chain bulletin); Wall Street Journal (13 Nov 2026), via Newsmax wire on Yahoo News and Voice of Emirates; RFI via AOL (11 Nov 2026, Paris prosecutor’s warrant request); The Record (9 Nov 2026, French attribution and at least 15 fires); Insurance Journal, from Reuters (13 Nov 2026, BSI warning); Bytes Europe (13 Nov 2026, CCB warning); Midnight Blue (Nov 2026, AK-SM 800A research); GBHackers (13 Nov 2026); NPR (9 Nov 2026, Iranian denial); Iran International (14 Nov 2026, IRGC response); Arab News, from AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement) - Barrot: EU sanctions within a month 17–18 Nov 2026; EU confirms sanctions in preparation, French sanctions push and Health-ISAC bulletin 16 Nov 2026; WSJ report 13 Nov 2026; BSI and CCB warnings 13 Nov 2026; warrant request 11 Nov 2026; French attribution 9 Nov 2026; IRGC rejects French findings 14 Nov 2026; October attack 11–12 Oct 2026; investigations ongoing

item.title: [Critical] CISA and FBI warn of an ongoing threat to internet-connected refrigeration as European supermarket attacks reach at least 11 countries
item.category: Incident — CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT joint warning (5 Nov 2026) and a second wave of refrigeration attacks across about 11 European countries (1–4 Nov); Belgium says its evidence points to Iran (12 Nov), no formal attribution
item.description: Hackers are tampering with internet-connected refrigeration controllers in European supermarkets, and on 5 November CISA and the FBI, with HHS, USDA and DOT, warned the threat is ongoing and also reaches healthcare, chemical, transport and cold-storage operations. Hundreds of French stores were hit in October; a second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 countries, forcing units into continuous heating or defrost, and three French blood-service sites had settings changed with no blood lost. On 10 November Sweden warned that more incidents are likely after refrigeration was tampered with at seven Coop stores and an undisclosed number of ICA stores on 2 November; its NCSC says the victims mainly ran older systems from one manufacturer protected by weak passwords. On 12 November Belgium’s interior minister said evidence on the Belgian attacks points to Iran but stopped short of an official attribution (see top story); a pro-Russian claim is unverified, and France has formally attributed only the separate 12 October attack, to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard. Exposure is falling but not gone: exposed Danfoss StoreView instances dropped from 3,004 to 708 between 9 October and 5 November (The Hacker News, 9 November). Sekoia reported on 10 November that the second wave used a non-public, unauthenticated flaw that renames the controller’s admin account, apparently a step towards resetting its password, and assesses that both waves may come from the same actor. If a controller is reachable from the internet, treat it as at risk today. - TechCrunch (5 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI joint statement); SentinelOne Labs (3 Nov 2026, updated 4 Nov); Cybersecurity Dive (3 Nov 2026, updated with 4 Nov developments); Unit 42 (6 Nov 2026, exposure counts); Censys (6 Nov 2026, exposure analysis); BleepingComputer (5 Nov 2026); Nextgov (29 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera (4 Nov 2026); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012; The Cyber Express (6 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory summary); Industrial Cyber (6 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (6 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (6 Nov 2026, hardening guidance); The Hacker News (9 Nov 2026, exposure trend); eBuilder Security (11 Nov 2026, Swedish government and NCSC warning); Arab News/AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement); Sekoia TDR (10 Nov 2026, second-wave technique) - Attacks overnight 1–2 Nov 2026; Germany, Romania and UK confirmed 4 Nov 2026; CISA/FBI joint warning 5 Nov 2026; French attribution of the October attack 9 Nov 2026; Swedish government warning 10 Nov 2026; Belgian minister points to Iran 12 Nov 2026 — investigations ongoing

item.title: [Critical] Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
item.category: Incident — PHP2Shell plus Gaia root flaw CVE-2026-123039 used to backdoor Check Point gateways and wipe a VMware ESXi host (wave 1 from 30 Oct, Israel; wave 2 from 2 Nov, multiple countries); CVE-2026-123039 added to CISA KEV 13 Nov 2026
item.description: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, about a week after fixes shipped, then used a local flaw in the gateway’s DynamicCLI service (CVE-2026-123039) to become root. They planted web shells and backdoors named TSGA and TSProxy, scanned the internal network, moved over SSH to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper that overwrites and deletes files. The first wave hit Israeli organizations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached gateways in several countries and sectors with no destruction seen. The backdoors resemble tooling linked to the China-nexus group UNC5221, but Check Point does not attribute the campaign with confidence. CISA added CVE-2026-123039 to KEV on 13 November. No OT victim is reported, but these firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary and ESXi hosts often run HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Check Point Research (12 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1154 (12 Nov 2026, updated 13 Nov); CISA KEV alert (13 Nov 2026); BleepingComputer (Nov 2026) - Wave 1 from 30 Oct 2026; wave 2 from 2 Nov 2026; research published 12 Nov 2026; KEV addition 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell chained with a Linux kernel flaw to root exposed PAN-OS firewalls, 23–24 Oct; OT vendor advisories 28–30 Oct; Siemens adds metering gateways 16 Nov
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified on 29 October that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October, then stole Active Directory credentials. Victims were in the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea. The OT exposure keeps widening: Siemens lists Spectrum Power grid-control systems and AMIS TS, and on 16 November added its WTV676 and WTV776 metering gateways (all versions, no fix), Schneider lists a Foxboro DCS server, and ABB lists Netcontrol RTUs and ASPECT gateways, several with no fix yet. Attribution is suspected, not confirmed, and no Siemens, Schneider or ABB product is reported exploited. No OT operator has been named, so treat this as an IT-to-OT boundary warning. - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026) and Infosecurity Magazine (30 Oct 2026), citing Dream; CISA KEV catalog (30 Oct 2026 release); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.4 (16 Nov 2026, WTV676/WTV776 added; V1.2 29 Oct 2026), SSA-566512 V1.1 (28 Oct 2026), SSA-019113 and SSA-082556; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); ABB Netcontrol and Arctic advisories (30 Oct 2026), ASPECT advisory (29 Oct 2026) and APROL SA26P015 (23 Oct 2026); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-127 and VDE-2026-137 - Root compromises 23–24 Oct 2026, verified by Unit 42 29 Oct 2026; KEV additions 26 and 28 Oct 2026; Siemens, Schneider and ABB updates 28–30 Oct 2026; Siemens metering gateways added 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] A malicious update to drone ground-control software disrupted operations at German defence supplier Quantum Systems, reports say
item.category: Incident — Supply-chain compromise reported at German drone maker Quantum Systems via a malicious QBase ground-control software update (detected late Oct; reported 13 Nov 2026); no attribution
item.description: Quantum Systems, a German maker of military reconnaissance drones, says it detected an incident in late October that was part of an active attack by “hostile actors,” and that it worked with authorities so its unmanned systems could safely resume operations. Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, citing internal sources, report that the attackers pushed a malicious update to QBase, the company’s ground-control and mission-planning software, from the vendor’s own update server; it is unclear how many customers installed it. The German armed forces reportedly grounded the company’s drones as a precaution and left them out of a recent exercise. The company believes it was targeted for supporting Ukraine but names no attacker. For OT owners the lesson is wider than defence: a vendor’s update channel for control or engineering software is a direct path onto operational systems (editorial assessment). - BleepingComputer (13 Nov 2026), citing Der Spiegel and the Financial Times and a Quantum Systems statement - Incident detected late Oct 2026; reported 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] A Chilean solar-and-battery plant is still off the grid nearly three months after a cyberattack, and lawmakers want answers
item.category: Incident — cyberattack forced Chile’s 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant and its battery system off the grid (attack 26 Aug 2026, forced disconnection 27 Aug); still offline per the 14 Nov 2026 grid-coordinator report; congressional information requests filed 11 Nov 2026; no attribution
item.description: The 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant in Chile’s Tarapacá region, with a 98 MW / 312 MWh battery system still in commissioning, has been disconnected from the national grid since late August after a cyberattack. Chile’s National Electric Coordinator triggered its disconnection protocol on 27 August after the owner reported the attack, and its 14 November daily report still lists both assets at zero availability under forced outage. The coordinator calls the case exceptional and is withholding details while it investigates. On 11 November a member of Congress asked the security and energy ministries whether the national cybersecurity agency was notified as Chilean law requires and which control systems were hit; no answer had been published by 16 November. The owner, entry route and affected systems are undisclosed. Two suspected attacks on plants in Coquimbo the next day were reportedly ruled out. For renewables operators, the lesson is how long a plant stays dark once it is pulled off the grid for safety and cannot be restored with confidence (editorial assessment). - ESS News / pv magazine (17 Nov 2026, citing Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional records); T13 (16 Nov 2026, in Spanish); pv magazine Latin America (16 Nov 2026, congressional requests, in Spanish) - Ongoing — still offline per 14 Nov 2026 coordinator report; congressional requests 11 Nov 2026; reported 16–17 Nov 2026; attack 26 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Equinor says the attack on its IT systems is not self-spreading and production continues normally, but gives no recovery timeline
item.category: Incident — Ongoing cyberattack on certain IT systems at Norway’s Equinor, disclosed 17 Nov 2026; company update 18 Nov 2026 says it is not self-spreading malware and production continues as normal; no attribution
item.description: Equinor, Norway’s state-controlled energy company and the largest supplier of pipeline gas to the EU, disclosed on the evening of 17 November that it was fighting an ongoing cyberattack against certain IT systems. In an update on the morning of 18 November it said it now has a clearer picture of how the attack was carried out and which systems are affected, that the attack is not a virus and cannot spread on its own, and that it has found no effect on employees, partners or suppliers. Oil and gas production continues as normal and the company still reports no sign of data theft. Work to remove the attackers and restore systems continues with national security authorities, and Equinor says it is too early to give a timeframe. It has not disclosed the entry route, the systems involved or the attacker. Nothing reported points to OT, but an active intrusion at a major upstream and gas-export operator is exactly when IT-to-OT boundaries get tested (editorial assessment). - Equinor statement (17 Nov 2026, 18:55 CET; update 18 Nov 2026, 09:47 CET); IBTimes UK (17 Nov 2026, citing NTB, NSM and NRK); Euronext/Reuters wire (17 Nov 2026); The Star, from Reuters (18 Nov 2026) - Disclosed 17 Nov 2026; company update 18 Nov 2026; attack still being removed

item.title: [High] Ransomware halts smart-meter production and shipments at Japan’s Osaki Electric
item.category: Incident — Ransomware at Japanese smart-meter maker Osaki Electric (confirmed 17 Nov 2026); production and shipments suspended at its Saitama centre and group plants (reported 18 Nov 2026); no group named
item.description: Osaki Electric, a Japanese maker of electricity smart meters, said ransomware encrypted data on its servers on 17 November. It confirmed the attack at about 10:35 a.m. local time, cut its systems off from outside networks around midday, and suspended production and shipments of smart meters and other products at its Saitama R&D and manufacturing centre and at group production companies Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platech. NHK reported on 18 November that the production-management system was among the systems knocked out. Outside specialists are checking whether data was stolen, and the company has informed police and customers. No group has claimed the attack and the entry route is not disclosed. Nothing reported suggests meters already in the field or electricity supply are affected. For utilities, the risk is supply-chain: delayed meter rollouts, and the question of how a supplier protects the systems that build, configure and sign the devices it ships (editorial assessment). - Osaki Electric announcement, via TipRanks (17 Nov 2026, updated 18 Nov 2026); NHK (18 Nov 2026, in Japanese); Kyodo, via Yahoo! Japan News and Tokyo Shimbun (18 Nov 2026, in Japanese) - Attack confirmed 17 Nov 2026; production and shipments still suspended per 18 Nov 2026 reports

item.title: [Medium] Infoblox confirms a breach through a migration vendor that reportedly exposed customer DNS and DHCP configuration snapshots
item.category: Incident — Supply-chain breach confirmed by Infoblox (16 Nov 2026): attackers used a compromised data-migration vendor’s access to pull data from Infoblox SharePoint, reportedly including customer NIOS configuration snapshots; no product or update compromise found so far
item.description: Infoblox, whose NIOS DNS, DHCP and IP-address-management appliances run in many utility, energy and manufacturing networks, confirmed on 16 November that attackers got in through an unnamed third-party data-migration vendor with trusted access to its Microsoft environment and pulled data from SharePoint. Reporting says the haul included configuration snapshots from some customers’ NIOS deployments, such as DNS and DHCP settings, Grid databases and reporting logs, along with employee records. No passwords or credentials were reportedly taken, and Infoblox says it has seen no sign that its products, cloud services or software updates were touched. For OT defenders the risk is reconnaissance: a configuration snapshot is a detailed map of internal hostnames, subnets and services that could help an attacker plan a route towards plant networks. - Security Affairs (17 Nov 2026), citing Infoblox and The Register - Infoblox confirmed breach 16 Nov 2026; reported 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] FBI warns that the ARTEX AI framework is automating intrusions at machine speed, with energy and manufacturing among the targets
item.category: Threat Intel — FBI FLASH (13 Nov 2026) on malicious use of ARTEX, an open-source AI agent framework that automates intrusions; energy and manufacturing among targeted sectors; no OT impact described
item.description: The FBI issued a FLASH alert on 13 November warning that several malicious actors are using ARTEX, an open-source framework that lets any large language model drive an intrusion, to automate the steps from reconnaissance through privilege escalation to data theft. In some cases attackers went from first targeting to privileged access in under three hours. Targeted sectors named include energy, manufacturing, telecommunications, defence, semiconductors and healthcare. The tool appeared on GitHub in August; the original repository has since been removed, but the FBI says forks, archived copies and a commercial version keep it in circulation, and Censys counted more than 1,600 internet-exposed ARTEX consoles. The FBI’s examples are IT intrusions, not control-system attacks, but a three-hour path to domain admin leaves little time to cut IT-to-OT links during an incident (editorial assessment). - FBI FLASH (13 Nov 2026), via The Record (13 Nov 2026); Viakoo Daily OT Security News via Security Boulevard (17 Nov 2026) - Published 13 Nov 2026; malicious use since at least August 2026

item.title: [Medium] Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware attacks on industrial organizations in Q3, up 11%, and found no case of an operator touching a control system
item.category: Research — Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis for Q3 2026 (published 16 Nov 2026), covering July–September; Check Point October 2026 statistics (12 Nov 2026) for comparison
item.description: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organizations between July and September 2026, up 11% on the second quarter, while the number of brands claiming industrial victims jumped from 70 to 99. Manufacturing took 69% of cases, followed by the ICS ecosystem of integrators, engineering firms and equipment makers (116) and transport and logistics (105); oil and gas logged 47. Qilin and The Gentlemen drove 29% of the total. Dragos saw no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: production stopped because the IT, ERP and virtualization layers plants rely on went down, as when Fairlife reportedly halted all four of its US plants for about 11 days. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. Check Point separately counted a record 1,063 claimed victims across all sectors in October. - Dragos (16 Nov 2026); Australian Cyber Security Magazine (17 Nov 2026); Check Point Research October 2026 statistics, via iTWire (12 Nov 2026) - Published 16 Nov 2026; data covers July–September 2026

item.title: [High] Hackers probe 14 newly disclosed flaws in end-of-life Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers, five of which will never be fixed
item.category: Advisory — 14 flaws in end-of-life Copeland (Dixell) XWEB EVO refrigeration supervisors disclosed by VulnCheck; CVE records published 12 Nov 2026 (incl. CVE-2026-124010, CVE-2026-124014); exploitation attempts seen within hours; five flaws will not be fixed
item.description: VulnCheck has disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in Copeland’s XWEB EVO, the Dixell supervisory system that runs supermarket and cold-storage refrigeration, each of which gave its researcher root on test units. Nine affect only firmware built before a 2021 rewrite and include unauthenticated command execution and a hard-coded admin password. The other five reach the latest firmware: the daily admin password is derived from the device’s MAC address and the date, and the MAC address is visible without logging in, so an attacker can compute the password, turn on SSH and log in as root. VulnCheck’s sensors saw exploitation attempts against two older-firmware flaws within two hours of the 12 November CVE publication; it calls the sources opportunistic scanners, not the state campaign in France. Copeland ended XWEB EVO support on 16 March 2026 and will not fix the five current-firmware flaws; nearly 2,000 units are reachable from the internet. CyberScoop adds that XBOW honeypots posing as these controllers drew hundreds of requests and login attempts within a day, and someone changed the temperature on one simulated freezer. - SecurityWeek (16 Nov 2026, VulnCheck research and exploitation telemetry; Copeland end-of-life notice); CyberScoop (13 Nov 2026, XBOW honeypot findings; Copeland statement); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 - CVE records published 12 Nov 2026; probing 12–13 Nov 2026; reported 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Six unpatched pre-login flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers prompt Belgian, German and Irish warnings to pull them off the internet
item.category: Advisory — Six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A (firmware up to 5.3.2), disclosed by Midnight Blue; Belgian CCB and German BSI warnings (13 Nov 2026), joined by Ireland’s NCSC; CVEs pending; no exploitation of these flaws reported
item.description: Amsterdam consultancy Midnight Blue has disclosed six stack buffer overflows in Danfoss AK-SM 800A system managers, the store-level controllers that run supermarket and cold-storage refrigeration, that allow remote code execution without logging in; one works even with “strict” session control turned on. All firmware up to 5.3.2 is affected and CVEs are still pending. The BSI says the 5.4.0 package released this month is not affected, but Midnight Blue says 5.4.0 predates its research and does not fix these bugs, so treat 5.4.0 as unconfirmed until Danfoss says otherwise. The researchers say an attacker could plant code that survives a factory reset or firmware update, or brick units, because the device does not appear to use secure boot; that is a stated possibility, not a demonstrated one. Belgium’s CCB and Germany’s BSI (13 November) and Ireland’s NCSC have all told operators that firmware updates, password changes and strict mode are not enough for internet-exposed units. Danfoss had published no advisory or fix date as of 16 November. No exploitation of these six flaws is reported. - Midnight Blue (Nov 2026); The Hacker News (16 Nov 2026, CCB, BSI and Irish NCSC warnings; Danfoss status); Bytes Europe (13 Nov 2026, CCB warning); Cyber Press (13 Nov 2026); Insurance Journal, from Reuters (13 Nov 2026, BSI warning); Filstalexpress (13 Nov 2026, BSI firmware details) - Status re-checked 16 Nov 2026 (no Danfoss fix); CCB and BSI warnings 13 Nov 2026; research published Nov 2026

item.title: [High] ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens finds the exploited Node2Shell bug in SIMATIC SCADA and PCS 7, and more OT vendors confirm PHP2Shell exposure
item.category: Advisory — ICS Patch Tuesday (11 Nov 2026): Siemens (9 advisories, 10 flaws, two on Node2Shell), Schneider Electric SEVD-2026-314-01, Johnson Controls, Hitachi Energy and Phoenix Contact; CERT@VDE (8 advisories incl. Helmholz, Weidmüller, Beckhoff) and Axis CVE-2026-13312 (10 Nov)
item.description: Siemens published nine advisories on 11 November covering ten flaws, two of them describing how the exploited Node2Shell (Brotli) bug reaches its products. High-severity issues touch SIMATIC SCADA and PCS 7, SIMATIC WinCC Graphics Designer, meta-iot2050, ROS#, Simcenter Femap and the Mendix Studio Pro MCP server, and could allow code injection or system compromise. Several products have no fix yet and some versions will not be fixed, so Siemens points customers to mitigations; it has seen Node2Shell exploitation attempts but no attacks aimed at its products. Schneider Electric fixed a medium-severity file-handling flaw in EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody, Johnson Controls fixed EasyIO Neo IO Manager and a C•CURE 9000/victor installer that could expose admin credentials, and Hitachi Energy and Phoenix Contact confirmed PHP2Shell impact. A day earlier CERT@VDE flagged a dozen bugs in Helmholz’s myREX24V2 remote-access server (fix 2.21.0) and two PHP2Shell use-after-free flaws in MB connect line’s mbCONNECT24/mymbCONNECT24 remote-maintenance portal that allow unauthenticated code execution (CVE-2026-109618, CVSS 3.1 9.8; CVE-2026-109619, 8.1; fixed in 2.21.6), and Axis rated a Camera Station flaw 9.9 (CVE-2026-13312). - CISA ICSA-26-316-01 to -05 (12 Nov 2026, Siemens building-automation, energy, Industrial Edge and RUGGEDCOM APE1808 advisories republished, incl. PHP2Shell impact); SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday roundup (11 Nov 2026); Siemens ProductCERT; Schneider Electric SEVD-2026-314-01; CERT@VDE VDE-2026-141 and VDE-2026-128 (10 Nov 2026); Axis CVE-2026-13312 advisory (10 Nov 2026) - Published 11 Nov 2026 (Siemens, Schneider, Johnson Controls, Hitachi Energy); 10 Nov 2026 (CERT@VDE, Axis)

item.title: [High] N-able ships Hotfix 3 for 17 more N-central flaws after attackers planted miners on servers already running Hotfix 2
item.category: Active exploitation — N-able N-central: 4EverAble2Shell exploited to plant miners (13 Nov 2026); N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and removes the Legacy API (16–17 Nov 2026)
item.description: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November, which it calls a critical security update. It fixes 17 new CVEs, including authentication bypasses, missing authorization checks, path traversal leading to code execution and a syslog injection that runs commands as root, and it removes the Legacy API option that the actively exploited 4EverAble2Shell chain depends on. On-premises servers need the upgrade now; hosted servers update automatically, but every customer must also upgrade Agents and Probes, which N-able warns can otherwise be impersonated. The fix follows Huntback’s 13 November finding of cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2. Remote control and Intune integration stay blocked for now. Many integrators manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools, and a miner today can be a hands-on intruder tomorrow (editorial assessment). - The Hacker News (17 Nov 2026, Hotfix 3, citing N-able release notes of 16 Nov); The Hacker News (13 Nov 2026, citing Huntback and Previdian); The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026, new chains); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Tenable (10 Nov 2026) - Hotfix 3 released 16 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 13 Nov 2026; Able2Shell disclosed 9 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] ConnectWise says ScreenConnect attacks continue against unpatched systems after rogue clients reached 288 endpoints at 48 organizations
item.category: Active campaign — rogue ScreenConnect clients and the SCKit toolkit pushed through hijacked partner panels (from 11 Nov 2026); ConnectWise closes its investigation and disables five extensions in 400 partner environments (16 Nov 2026)
item.description: ConnectWise said on 16 November that it has finished investigating unauthorized access to partner ScreenConnect environments, has remotely disabled five third-party extensions (Labtech Plus, RMM Plus, RMM+ and two password-link variants) across 400 partner environments, and wants technician clients on version 26.6.5 or later. That version fixes CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9), which can let files be pushed and run through a live session without the host’s approval. Attackers are suspected of abusing an authentication flaw in RMM+ 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 to run commands and install rogue clients and SCKit, a toolkit built to jump from customer machines to technicians’ computers; Huntress counted at least 288 endpoints at 48 organizations, and separately reported that attacker guest sessions have sent about 688,000 “run file” requests to 42 MSP servers since 20 October, waiting for any unpatched technician to join. ConnectWise stresses that disabling extensions and updating does not remove access an intruder already has. Many integrators support plant systems through ScreenConnect, so a compromised technician is a direct path into OT (editorial assessment). - The Hacker News (17 Nov 2026, ConnectWise update); Huntress (16 Nov 2026, CVE-2026-84869 spray campaign; 12 Nov 2026, rogue clients); SecurityWeek (17 Nov 2026); Blackpoint Cyber via The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026); The Register (12 Nov 2026); ConnectWise advisory - ConnectWise update and Huntress spray-campaign report 16 Nov 2026; reported 17 Nov 2026; activity detected 11 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] CISA flags six flaws in Dorsett InfoScan water-utility SCADA and republishes a batch of Siemens advisories
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS advisory batch, 17 Nov 2026: Dorsett Controls InfoScan (ICSA-26-321-01, water sector, highest CVSS v3.1 8.1 / v4 8.5) plus Siemens republications incl. SIMATIC, SIMATIC WinCC, RUGGEDCOM APE1808, Mendix Studio Pro, Simcenter Femap, meta-iot2050, ROS# and the SIMATIC S7 Webserver API .NET library (ICSA-26-321-02)
item.description: CISA’s 17 November ICS release leads with Dorsett Controls InfoScan, a SCADA and telemetry platform tagged for the water and wastewater sector. Versions 1.45.0 and earlier carry six flaws, the worst a TLS certificate-validation weakness (CVSS v3.1 8.1) that could let an attacker in the network path intercept or tamper with traffic; the others include hard-coded encryption keys, a template endpoint with no authentication, and unauthenticated endpoints that leak system details. Dorsett fixed them in version 1.46. The rest of the batch republishes Siemens ProductCERT advisories, among them the SIMATIC S7 Webserver API .NET client library, where a path-traversal flaw needs version 3.3.61 and an information leak needs 3.3.62. CISA reports no known public exploitation of any of these. - CISA ICSA-26-321-01 (Dorsett Controls InfoScan) and ICSA-26-321-02 to -11 (Siemens); WindowsForum (17 Nov 2026, InfoScan and S7 .NET library summaries); Siemens ProductCERT SSA-390352 - Published 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] Comments close 30 November on NIST’s draft rewrite of its OT security guide, which adds water, food, rail, maritime and building-automation coverage
item.category: Guidance — NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 4 draft (released 21 Sep 2026); public comments close 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST’s draft Revision 4 of SP 800-82, the US government’s main guide to operational technology security, is open for public comment until 30 November 2026. The draft reorganises the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with risk management now led by the Govern function, and adds sector material for building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels, and industrial IoT connected to cloud services. It also expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and detection, protecting system-management functions, and applying zero-trust principles. Many regulators, insurers and auditors use 800-82 as a reference, so its final wording can shape what operators are asked to show; the comment window is the chance for practitioners to flag guidance that would not work on a plant floor. - NIST CSRC, SP 800-82 Rev. 4 initial public draft (21 Sep 2026); SecurityWeek (24 Sep 2026) - Forward-looking: public comments close 30 Nov 2026
